findings.title: translate() only lazy-loads the current locale, not the new fallback locales
findings.body: Translations are loaded lazily per locale (`load_locale`). `translate` still only guarantees `config.locale` is loaded. Now that `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks` is enabled and `FallbackLocaleList#[]` returns `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale, :en]`, a lookup that misses in the current locale will consult locales whose YAML may never have been loaded, so the fallback silently fails and `I18n.t` returns "translation missing". The only place that pre-loads the fallback chain is `ApplicationController#set_locale`, so every non-request code path is broken: Sidekiq jobs, mailers/notification emails rendered with the recipient's locale, rake tasks, the console, and any `I18n.with_locale` block. Worse, because `translate` memoizes no-arg lookups in the process-wide LRU cache, the bogus "translation missing" value is cached under that key and keeps being returned even after the fallback locale is eventually loaded. `translate` should ensure the whole `I18n.fallbacks[config.locale]` chain is loaded (or `ensure_loaded!` should be called from a lower-level hook than the controller filter).

findings.title: LRU translation cache key does not include the fallback chain / SiteSetting.default_locale
findings.body: The cache key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`, but with the new fallbacks the resolved value for a given (key, locale) pair now also depends on `SiteSetting.default_locale`, which is per-site and mutable. `@cache` is an ivar on the `I18n` module singleton, i.e. shared by every site served by the process. In a multisite install, site A (default_locale `fr`) looking up a key that is missing in `de` will cache the French string under `key+de`, and site B (default_locale `en`) will then serve that French string to its German users — cross-tenant content leakage. Even single-site, changing the `default_locale` setting does not invalidate these entries, so stale fallback translations persist until the process is restarted. The key must incorporate the fallback chain (or the cache must be reset when `default_locale` changes / be per-site).

findings.title: Fallback lookup hits SiteSetting and allocates on every translation
findings.body: `I18n::Backend::Fallbacks#translate` calls `I18n.fallbacks[locale]` on every single translation. The stock `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks` memoizes the computed chain in the Hash; this override replaces `Hash#[]` and never stores anything, so each call performs a `SiteSetting.default_locale` read plus `to_sym`, `uniq`, `compact` and a fresh Array allocation. Every interpolated/pluralized lookup (`args.length > 0` bypasses the LRU cache in translate_accelerator) therefore pays this cost, which defeats part of the purpose of the translation accelerator. Memoize per locale and invalidate when `default_locale` changes.

findings.title: Every request depends on a method that only exists on the custom fallbacks object
findings.body: `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only defined on `FallbackLocaleList`, the object assigned in `config/initializers/i18n.rb`. Rails' `I18n::Railtie.initialize_i18n` runs in `after_initialize` (i.e. after config/initializers) and, if `config.i18n.fallbacks` is truthy anywhere, executes `I18n.fallbacks = I18n::Locale::Fallbacks.new(...)`, silently replacing the custom object. Any plugin, environment file, or someone re-adding the line this PR just deleted from production.rb/profile.rb would then make this `before_filter` raise `NoMethodError` on every request — a full site outage, and only in that environment. Either define `ensure_loaded!` on `I18n` itself (next to `I18n.ensure_loaded!`) or guard with `respond_to?`.

findings.title: New fallback behaviour has no tests and silently enables fallbacks in dev/test
findings.body: Fallbacks were previously enabled only in production/profile/cloud66 via `config.i18n.fallbacks = true`; moving the setup into `config/initializers/i18n.rb` enables them in development and test too. That changes existing behaviour: specs (and developers) that previously saw "translation missing" for keys absent from a non-English locale will now silently get English text, so missing-translation regressions stop being detectable. No spec is added for the new `FallbackLocaleList` ordering (user locale → site default → :en), for `ensure_loaded!`, or for the lazy-loading interaction with fallbacks, which is where the real risk is (see the unloaded-fallback-locale problem in translate_accelerator).

findings.title: @loaded_locales initialized outside LOAD_MUTEX in ensure_loaded!
findings.body: `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales ||= []` outside `LOAD_MUTEX`, while `load_locale` mutates and reads the same array inside the mutex and `translate` reads it without the mutex. Two threads entering `ensure_loaded!` concurrently when the ivar is nil can each assign a different array, so one thread's `@loaded_locales << locale` is lost; the subsequent `@loaded_locales.empty?` check in `load_locale` can then re-load all `.rb` locale files and re-load an already loaded locale. Initialize the array inside the mutex (or at boot) to keep the bookkeeping consistent.

findings.title: `uniq.compact` cannot protect against a nil default_locale, and the chain depends on the DB
findings.body: `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en].uniq.compact` calls `to_sym` on the setting before `compact` can run, so if `SiteSetting.default_locale` ever returns nil this raises `NoMethodError` from inside an `I18n.t` call rather than falling back — the `compact` is dead code for that case. More generally, every translation now requires a readable `site_settings` state; in contexts where the DB/SiteSetting is unavailable (asset precompile without a DB, very early boot, error pages rendered while the DB is down) an `I18n.t` call will now blow up instead of returning a translation. Guard the setting read (`SiteSetting.default_locale.presence&.to_sym` plus a rescue).
